question.problem: Given that  $\operatorname{log}⁡(10-4x)=\operatorname{log}⁡(10-3x)$, what is the value of $x?$
question.worked_solution:
Since the logarithms on both sides of the equation have the same base, we can equate the arguments. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{log}⁡(10-4x) & =\operatorname{log}⁡(10-3x) \\ 10-4x & =10-3x \\ x & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now check for extraneous solutions by substituting back into the original equation: 

- Substituting $x=0$ back into the original equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{log}⁡(10-4(0)) & \overset{?}{=}\operatorname{log}⁡(10-3(0)) \\ \operatorname{log}⁡(10) & =\operatorname{log}⁡(10)\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=0$ is a valid solution.
